title: India-Pakistan World Cup Clash Draws 8.4 Million Ticket Requests as Ballot Tops 120 Million
excerpt: The October 10, 2027 match at the Wanderers has 8,397,294 applications for a 34,000-seat stadium. The free ballot closes on November 21 — fans who miss it cannot buy through the ballot at all.
body:
• The India versus Pakistan group match on October 10, 2027 at the Wanderers Stadium in Johannesburg has received 8,397,294 ticket requests, the ICC said.
  • Total ballot requests have passed 120 million (120,809,467 as of November 1), from 2.8 million unique fans in 193 countries.
  • The final, on November 21 at the same venue, is close behind with 7,900,944 requests.
  • For diaspora fans: entry to the ballot is free at tickets.cricketworldcup.com until 23:59 CAT on November 21, and fans who do not register in this window will not be eligible to buy through the ballot once it closes.

Nearly 8.4 million ticket applications have been received for India and Pakistan's group-stage clash at next year's Men's Cricket World Cup, organisers said on Monday, according to Reuters. The rivals meet in Johannesburg at the Wanderers on October 10, 2027, in a stadium Reuters put at 34,000 seats.

The ICC put the exact figure at 8,397,294 requests for that one match. The final, scheduled for November 21 at the same venue, is trailing close behind with 7,900,944 requests.

Demand across the tournament

Total ticket requests have surpassed 120 million — 120,809,467 applications as of November 1 — from 2.8 million unique fans in 193 countries, the ICC said. More than 32 million match registrations have been completed, which the ICC said shows demand is not limited to the highest-profile fixtures.

Fans from South Africa, the United Kingdom, India, the United States and Australia lead the ballot registrations. The 41 fixtures hosted across eight venues in South Africa have attracted more than 105 million applications, and matches involving South Africa have amassed nearly 26 million requests. In Zimbabwe, the tally has crossed 13 million (13,350,190), led by just over 3.3 million requests for Zimbabwe versus India on October 24 at the new Mosi-oa-Tunya International Cricket Stadium in Victoria Falls. Namibia's six fixtures in Windhoek have drawn more than two million requests.

"The response to the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2027 has been outstanding. This level of demand reflects the global appeal of the tournament and the significance of bringing the Men's Cricket World Cup back to Africa for the first time in 24 years."

— Gaurav Saxena, ICC General Manager, Events and Cricket Operations

How the ballot works

Entry into the ticket ballot is free and no payment is taken at registration, the ICC said. Fans can submit one ballot entry per person, per match, and may enter for multiple matches. The ballot is not first-come, first-served, so entering at any point in the window carries the same chance. Where demand exceeds the available allocation, access to buy tickets is decided by a randomised ballot, and successful and unsuccessful applicants are contacted by email.

The tournament runs from October 2 to November 21, 2027, with 57 matches across 12 venues, co-hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. It is the first Men's World Cup in Africa in 24 years, and Namibia will stage World Cup matches for the first time.

What fans should do

Register before the window closes at 23:59 CAT on November 21 at tickets.cricketworldcup.com: create an account, select preferred matches, and submit. The ICC is explicit that fans who do not register during the ballot window will not be eligible to access tickets through this ballot once it closes.
